Many tech giants are eager to pay for these upgrades to power AI. Increasing production from existing nuclear plants will add an estimated 6,000 to 8,000 megawatts of electric capacity to US grids.

infosec.title: 250,000 Impacted by Data Breaches at New Jersey, Texas Healthcare Firms
infosec.summary: Clover Health Investments said attackers used social engineering to compromise three employee accounts, exposing data on 138,677 people. AngMar Management Services found stolen patient data after suspicious activity, affecting 126,196 people. Exposed records included Social Security numbers, diagnoses, medical histories, insurance details, prescriptions, and service dates. The Interlock ransomware group claimed to have stolen 700 gigabytes from AngMar.

infosec.title: Citrix NetScaler security snafus get even worse amid more 0-day reports
infosec.summary: A single crafted request knocks NetScaler ADC and Gateway appliances offline through CVE-2026-88779, a memory overflow zero-day affecting deployments configured as a SAML service provider or identity provider. CISA confirmed active exploitation, and watchTowr told The Register it suspects attackers are crashing appliances deliberately to speed up exploitation of CVE-2026-88771, one of eight NetScaler bugs disclosed September 27. Apply Citrix's fixed build or interim mitigation, starting with Gateway and AAA virtual servers that have SAML enabled, and run Citrix's IOC script while treating a clean result as inconclusive.

infosec.title: CVE-2026-19444: How copying in kubectl breaks trust
infosec.summary: A malicious container can write files anywhere a Windows user's account can reach, including the Startup folder, when that user runs kubectl cp against it (CVE-2026-19444, CVSS 6.5). kubectl cp unpacks the output of whatever tar binary the container ships, and the entry-path check added after three 2019 CVEs never accounted for Windows path separators. Windows clients need kubectl v1.36.5, v1.35.9, or v1.34.12, since the flaw is in client-side extraction and the cluster version does not matter.

infosec.title: WordPress libheif RCE: Exploit Chain
infosec.summary: Fortbridge has published the first public exploit chain for a libheif heap overflow (GHSA-x8r2-mggj-j6wr) originally discovered by Alex Thomas and Wordfence. By uploading crafted HEIC images via the WordPress Media Library, an authenticated attacker can defeat ASLR using pixel values in generated JPEGs and hijack a C++ virtual table pointer to achieve remote code execution. Administrators should update libheif to 1.23.3, disable unused HEIC/AVIF uploads, and treat repeated PHP-FPM 503 errors on image uploads as security events.

infosec.title: MALFEX npm Malware Campaign: Three Payloads And An Adversary That Signs Their Work
infosec.summary: MALFEX, an npm campaign run by a single operator, published eight malicious packages that targeted Windows systems. Its payloads included Overlord RAT and movinlike, a stealer that took Discord tokens, browser credentials, Telegram sessions, and cryptocurrency wallets. Three packages remain installable (function-flag, function-color, and cdn-img-fetch), and the first two have no advisory.

infosec.title: A Vault with a Heap-View: The Uncomfortable Space Between AgentCore Harness and Identity
infosec.summary: AWS AgentCore Harness is an agentic service and AgentCore Identity is a service that provides agents with identities. Unit 42 discovered that the bash tool that is enabled by default on AgentCore agents runs arbitrary bash commands and code as root. Using this primitive, the researchers demonstrated that they could exfiltrate the AgentCore Identity JWT by scanning the heap for it and then exfiltrating it.

infosec.title: gdp-ts
infosec.summary: gdp-ts is a TypeScript library, linter, and agent skill that turns skipped or mismatched authorization checks into compile errors. Sensitive functions demand a type-level proof, minted only by a trusted check module, that this exact user was authorized for this exact resource, with near-zero runtime cost. A lint preset blocks forged proofs via as casts, and the bundled skill steers coding agents toward the pattern.

infosec.title: mcpward
infosec.summary: mcpward pins an MCP server's tool contract to a committed lockfile and fails CI when it drifts, catching silently rewritten descriptions (rug-pulls), readOnlyHint flips, and breaking schema changes. It works black-box against any stdio or HTTP server and runs fully offline with no account or telemetry, unlike Snyk Agent Scan. It also flags tool-poisoning patterns such as injection phrasing and hidden Unicode, with output to SARIF, JUnit, or a PR comment.

infosec.title: PoC Index
infosec.summary: Search 82,000+ public CVE proof-of-concept exploits from GitHub, Nuclei, ExploitDB, Metasploit, and Vulhub.

infosec.title: MCP for agent-to-agent comms may be the riskiest protocol you've never heard of
infosec.summary: Google and four other organizations acknowledged flaws over the past five months where a prompt injection landing on one AI agent over MCP was forwarded to other internal agents, which executed it on trust. Researcher Syed Anas Mohiuddin named the technique "protocol pivoting," though X41 D-Sec's Markus Vervier told Ars Technica it is plain indirect prompt injection. The bugs typically ended in SSRF, ranging from severity 2.7 at Rapid7 (CVE-2026-97228) to 8 in Google's mcp-toolbox, which followed redirects without validating target IPs.

infosec.title: NTS: Authenticated Time at Meta
infosec.summary: Meta added Network Time Security (RFC 8915) to its public time service at nts.meta.com, so on-path attackers can no longer forge the clock that certificate, token, and replay-window checks rely on. Its servers hold no per-client state because each one derives the cookie-sealing key from a shared master secret and the Unix epoch day using HKDF-SHA256. NTS does not stop delay attacks or prevent an authenticated server from being simply wrong, and the stock Android and iOS time clients still sync over unauthenticated packets.

infosec.title: Is Sandboxing Sufficient to Contain Rogue Agents?
infosec.summary: When discussing the OpenAI and other agent escapes, the conversation inevitably turns to discussing sandboxes. OpenAI has not demonstrated to this point a serious containment strategy, so this discussion may hold weight. However, sandboxes are not sufficient as useful agents need Internet access as well as the fact that agents are potentially overeager.

design.title: Capcom Plans to Use AI to Speed up the Game Development Process
design.summary: Capcom intends to use AI to speed up game development through REX, a major overhaul of its RE Engine meant to create a "game engine of the AI generation." Programmer Satoshi Ishida said AI would mainly streamline workflows, since larger games and assets have lengthened development times. Capcom had earlier said AI would assist with graphics, sound and programming, while AI-generated content would stay out of its games.

design.title: Redesigned MacBook Pro with OLED to feature ‘significantly lighter' design
design.summary: Apple's upcoming MacBook Pro redesign will reportedly be significantly lighter thanks to miniaturized parts and a rearranged internal architecture, addressing the substantial weight of current models, particularly the 16-inch version. The overhaul is also expected to introduce Tandem OLED displays, touchscreens, and a Dynamic Island, with macOS Golden Gate receiving changes to support the new interactions. The M5 Pro and M5 Max models are expected to launch by November, as Apple reportedly skips higher-end M6 chips to accelerate its transition to M7.

design.title: OpenAI is adding invisible watermarks to ChatGPT and Codex for users in the EU
design.summary: OpenAI will begin adding invisible, machine-readable watermarks called textGrain to eligible ChatGPT and Codex output in the EU to comply with transparency requirements in the EU AI Act. The technology embeds a statistical pattern into generated language rather than adding hidden characters. API customers worldwide can optionally enable it for supported models. OpenAI acknowledges that watermarking remains imperfect because editing and short outputs can weaken the detectable signal.

design.title: Designing for Voice First
design.summary: Designing a voice-first app is hard because touch-and-typing workflows get decided first, leaving speech as another way to fill in the same fields. Five principles guide it: make spoken context count, let people steer as they think, show understanding, make correction easy, and let attention come and go. Voice should survive the shift from desk to AirPods and dog walks, so a returning user sees what happened and what still needs them.

design.title: Designing for People Who are Color Blind
design.summary: Color blindness affects about one in 12 men and one in 200 women, making key information, interactive elements, and color-coded data harder to perceive. Designs should pair color with an icon, pattern, or text label per WCAG 1.4.1, keep sufficient contrast, and avoid red-green and purple-blue pairings. Blue is a safer hue, though not guaranteed. Grayscale checks help, and hover, focus, and disabled states need non-color cues, ideally tested with real people.

design.title: AI invasive design
design.summary: Treating “AI native” as a mandate to maximize AI usage risks replacing valuable existing interactions simply to make products appear technologically current. A better approach treats human behavior as the ecosystem and asks AI to fit naturally within it by reflecting intent, providing adaptable scaffolding, maintaining consistent mental models, and scaling work without overwhelming people. Successful AI products should also preserve human participation and skills, because excessive automation can erode motivation, competence, and the value users get from doing meaningful work themselves.

design.title: Dot Matrix Loaders for Every App
design.summary: 55+ free and open-source loaders, built with React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and shadcn.

design.title: The First Collaborative Design Agent Workspace
design.summary: Open-source vibe design workspace & Claude Design alternative — build prototypes, landing pages, dashboards, slides, and HTML video with your own coding agent.

design.title: Ultra-Fast Zero-Dependency Shaders for Your Designs
design.summary: Zero-dependency canvas shaders that can be installed from npm or designed in Paper.

design.title: You can't describe your way to great design
design.summary: Prompt-driven AI tools force creative work into a describe-generate-evaluate loop that poorly supports the instinctive experimentation and continuous manipulation involved in serious design. Current tools tend to offer either editable but constrained output or expressive but largely fixed results, leaving professionals without the combination of creative range and direct control they need. Better AI creative tools should behave more like canvases where people can manipulate generated material fluidly, preserve editability, explore alternatives, and remain actively involved in shaping the work.

design.title: What the 500 in Blue-500 Means
design.summary: Numbers in color scales such as blue-500 may look standardized, but different design systems use them to represent entirely different concepts, including position in a ramp, guaranteed contrast relationships, measured lightness, or semantic roles. Material Design's original 50–900 scale primarily described positions and established 500 as a typical primary color, while systems such as Carbon, Material 3, and Radix give their numbers more explicit meaning. Understanding what a scale actually encodes is important because two colors carrying the same numerical label can have very different lightness, contrast, and intended uses.

design.title: Textile Artist Kathrin Marchenko Reimagines Iconic Monet Painting
design.summary: Kathrin Marchenko's embroidery Beyond the Bridge reimagines Monet's Bridge over a Pond of Water Lilies in wool and mohair thread on framed tulle, showing how closely brushstrokes and stitches relate.

design.title: The Top 10 Graphic Design Trends for 2027 Are About Process, Not AI
design.summary: Graphic design trends for 2027 favor provable craft over cheap AI polish, ranked by current visibility and growth speed through a "Heat-and-Slope Test."

marketing.title: You have a website. Cool. Is it growing?
marketing.summary: If your website isn't structured to be read, ranked, and cited, you're not in the conversation. Your prompt tracker gives you a number. Your content tool gives you another draft. You're still stuck figuring out what buyers ask, where competitors beat you, and what to publish next. GrowthX connects all three in a question map. See the questions that matter, where you show up in AI answers, and which pages to create or refresh to win them. Stop collecting scores. Start becoming the answer. Get your question map. Schedule time now!

marketing.title: The evidence is clear: AI search is costing publishers
marketing.summary: AI search is reducing the traffic publishers receive from traditional search while AI referrals remain too small to make up the difference. One study found AI Overviews reduced outbound organic clicks by 39.8%. Pew found traditional-result clicks fell from 15% to 8% when an AI summary appeared. Meanwhile, ChatGPT generated just 0.02% of publisher referrals compared with 7.3% from Google Search.

marketing.title: TikTok's Agent Checkout Enters the Race
marketing.summary: TikTok announced Shopping Assistant and Buy Direct at Advertising Week NYC on October 5, both now in eligibility-based testing in the US. Shopping Assistant is a conversational agent that handles product details, sizing, and availability, then hands the purchase to the in-app browser. Buy Direct is a one-click checkout inside the For You feed using stored payment and address details. Both run on Google's Universal Commerce Protocol, and the brand remains the merchant of record.

marketing.title: When to do sales remotely vs in-person
marketing.summary: The best mix of remote and in-person sales meetings depends on product complexity. Using the right mix can improve sales performance by up to 27.3%. For simple products, about 37.9% of meetings held in person produced the best results, while complex products performed worse when sales teams relied only on remote meetings. In-person meetings help build trust and uncover customer needs, which matters more when products require more customization or evaluation. Sales teams should use more in-person meetings early in complex sales relationships, then reduce them as they learn the customer's needs, while still accommodating customers who prefer remote meetings.

marketing.title: 5 tips for optimizing existing content for ChatGPT
marketing.summary: Existing content can be optimized for ChatGPT without publishing new posts. Lead with the answer before adding context so key claims are easier to extract. Use clear statements instead of hedging. Mention relevant brands and competitors to provide useful context. Turn headings into specific questions that mirror user queries. Refresh old posts with new data, screenshots, and sections rather than simply changing the publication date.

marketing.title: 4 SEO strategies for AI-driven brand search
marketing.summary: Google now shows AI Overviews for roughly 80% of branded searches. Keep brand messaging consistent across owned channels so AI systems get clear context, then create content to fill gaps where third-party sources currently shape answers. Monitor competitor content and review sites because negative claims can influence AI-generated brand answers. An accurate AI instructions page can also provide a direct source for brand information and become a frequently cited page in AI Overviews and AI Mode.

marketing.title: LinkedIn beats YouTube for B2B video, per Wistia's 2026 Report
marketing.summary: Wistia's 6th annual 2026 State of Video Report is here! Find out what 13 million video and 1,000 video marketers reveal about budgets, performance, and the impact of AI. Also - get benchmarks that can help you answer the age-old question: is this video actually working? Get your free copy here

marketing.title: How to write a great experiment plan
marketing.summary: An experiment plan should prevent costly errors, not serve as a ceremony. Start with an evidence-based hypothesis and one primary metric, then size the test around the smallest change worth shipping. Count only users who reached the change, since including everyone assigned dilutes the effect. Before launch, agree on stopping thresholds and on what happens under each outcome, so that early peeks don't drive the decision. After launch, confirm the traffic split holds.

marketing.title: SEO Audit Console - the technical SEO audit MCP server for Claude
marketing.summary: SEO Audit Console is an open-source MCP server that runs a technical SEO audit inside Claude by joining Search Console history with a live site crawl. It runs 99 checks and ranks findings by the clicks a fix could recover rather than by severity. It also writes paste-ready fixes such as 301 rules, JSON-LD, and internal links. The core audit needs only a Search Console service account and stores data locally.

marketing.title: Adam Harris on Why Follower Count Is the New Nielsen Box
marketing.summary: Follower count is becoming a poor measure of creator value as platforms increasingly serve content based on interests rather than follows. Adam Harris, co-founder of creator platform Gaggl, says 70% of video views now come from non-followers. Gaggl's campaign data also shows micro-creators generate 5X more engagement than larger creators. Larger creators remain useful for awareness while smaller creators drive deeper engagement. Harris recommends starting with small creator tests before scaling based on results.

marketing.title: How to survive a double life as an operator-creator
marketing.summary: Operator-creators run a flywheel where the day job makes the content credible and the audience becomes a distribution channel for the employer. Elena Verna keeps it working by disclosing everything to her employer, audience, and sponsors, ideally before the first day of work. She also sets boundaries up front, keeping the audience as her own while giving Lovable work first claim on her time.

marketing.title: LLMs are quietly watermarking AI content. Now what?
marketing.summary: AI labs are watermarking generated content by subtly changing word choices during generation. These tiny changes accumulate across longer outputs and can survive copy-paste and light edits. The bigger concern is AEO because labs may filter AI-generated content from training data to avoid model degradation. Teams should monitor branded and non-branded AI prompts to separate retrieved from trained-in visibility. Audit how much content is fully AI-generated and prioritize human rewriting for content that needs to influence future model knowledge.

marketing.title: 10 Halloween emails from last year to inspire your campaigns
marketing.summary: Halloween email inspo from Uber, Rest, and TUSHY.

marketing.title: I edit 115+ articles per year. Here are the 5 ways I edit drafts
marketing.summary: Semrush's senior blog editor shares her editing best practices, from fact-checking to giving more feedback than you think you should.

founders.title: Make business money move faster
founders.summary: Your business moves quickly. Your money should, too. Stripe Treasury brings payments and financial tools together, helping you pay vendors, send payouts, issue cards, and manage cash flow with less complexity. Instead of stitching together separate systems, your team can manage more financial workflows on the platform you already use for payments. That means less time navigating disconnected tools and more time focused on your business. From everyday operations to your next stage of growth, Stripe Treasury gives you flexible infrastructure to move money faster, streamline how work gets done, and build financial operations that can adapt as you scale. Explore Stripe Treasury

founders.title: Everyone is building the same thing
founders.summary: AI startups are converging on the same agent loops, memory systems, connectors, and sandboxes. The comparison here is to web companies in 2005, when everyone needed a database and a login page. Sharing those parts didn't make the businesses interchangeable. The concern is that founders are pitching basic infrastructure as their advantage while saying little about the customer problem they've figured out. Customer references and the team's knowledge of its industry may tell you more than which model or memory system they've chosen.

founders.title: Businesses are changing AI model providers more often
founders.summary: The monthly share of firms switching providers, averaged over three months, reached a record 8% in September. Anthropic gained significant share in May last year following the launches of Opus 4 and Sonnet 4. Switching declined over the next year until OpenAI introduced price cuts and new model launches in June this year. The intense competition between the two companies could be an early sign that AI models are becoming commodities.

founders.title: Platforms are (still) the best businesses
founders.summary: Businesses that perform strongly in profitability, scalability, and defensibility generate substantial profits relative to the capital they require. They grow with limited incremental effort or additional capital, and can sustain success over long periods. Platforms, businesses that enable direct interactions between customers, come closer to this Platonic ideal than any other type of business. Network effects and asset-light cost structures allow successful platforms to generate exceptional returns on invested capital.

founders.title: How to Hire in the Age of AI
founders.summary: While everyone agrees that AI requires rethinking which knowledge and skills signal quality in a new hire, there's little consensus on what those are. The stakes are highest for early-stage companies where new hires matter most. This post approaches the problem by running an experiment to see what makes the most sense for gauging a candidate's quality.

founders.title: GTM in git
founders.summary: Put as much of your GTM operations into git so agents can reason over them, test, and scale. Give agents the context and tools to understand the system, investigate a problem, and help implement a change. Agents make analysis easier to produce, so business context and tools need to work across interfaces, with evals to check that answers remain consistent. Every GTM operator needs reliable data, research, and an environment to make decisions quickly. Do as much GTM operating work as possible with coding agents, and keep the logical brain in git.

founders.title: What do you do the week a competitor raises millions?
founders.summary: A competitor raises millions, and suddenly you're considering a new round or copying features you'd ignored last week. Before changing either plan, look at what the money commits them to spending and how much growth they'll need to justify it. One founder in this piece calmed down after comparing their monthly burn with his own. Its review of ten AI categories found the best-funded company led three, with two already ahead before raising the most.

founders.title: Find the domain that matches your vision
founders.summary: Launching or rebranding? Explore DomainNames.com, the ultra-premium marketplace powered by GoDaddy. With over $2 billion in domains brokered, our team negotiates anonymously to help you acquire the right name, even if it's already taken. → Browse premium domains → Talk to a broker

founders.title: Higgsfield Ads Studio
founders.summary: Higgsfield Ads Studio produces static ads for every product on a website. Users just paste a link to their website, and it builds ads based on what converts in that niche. Ads produced by Higgsfield can be used in organic posts and paid campaigns. Users can review and fix logos, colors, tone, and selling points before ad generation.

founders.title: Claude now works with Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides
founders.summary: Claude for Google Workspace is now in public beta on all paid Claude plans. It adds Claude to Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides so users can work with Claude directly in their files. Anthropic has also released new Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides connectors so Claude users can create and edit Google files directly from Claude.

founders.title: Inference Is the Most Important Market in Software
founders.summary: AI inference is projected to become a $350 billion market by 2027, doubling the size of the database market. This shift leads to higher usage costs, reduced gross margins below typical SaaS levels, and makes infrastructure a key component of COGS. Businesses will need to adapt by optimizing efficiencies and could see innovation opportunities arise from these evolving dynamics.

founders.title: Will agents have network effects?
founders.summary: If my agent can email yours, why do we need to use the same product? That gives assistants a different problem from social networks, where everyone benefits from joining the same service. Network effects could still come from what agents create and share. An event website can bring in new users, and a shared reputation system could help agents find a trustworthy seller or a candidate who isn't publicly job hunting. That reputation system could belong to one assistant, or become a separate service that every assistant can access.

founders.summary: Years ago, Doron Merdinger started Doroni around a car-sized aircraft you could own. Currently 16,000+ investors, $45,000,000 raised, and 600+ pre-orders. Invest at $3.30/share before 10/23.

founders.title: Awkward Adolescence
founders.summary: Zappos had about five years with little competition because people doubted customers would buy shoes without trying them on.

founders.title: The single best predictor of founder success we've seen, above all else, is raw determination.
founders.summary: Interviews with more than 100 successful founders point to seven signs of determination, including earlier failures, rejection, and staying optimistic after losing a key employee or customer.

founders.title: Early Apple Retention Messaging benchmarks from 22M messages
founders.summary: Across 309 apps, subscribers accepted 0.68% of cancellation-screen discounts and 0.52% of plan switches, while the early observational data showed no measurable effect on cancellation rates.

founders.title: More warm bodies
founders.summary: As AI takes over routine work, one way to judge a role is to ask what its best performers did that went against the playbook.

crypto.title: Treasury withdraws crypto mixing rule
crypto.summary: FinCEN is withdrawing its 2023 proposal that would have designated international crypto mixing a "primary money laundering concern" under Section 311, along with a 2020 proposal requiring banks and money services businesses to verify identities and keep records on self-hosted wallet transactions above $3,000. The agency said commenters' concerns about the mixing rule's broad definition chilling legitimate privacy use informed the decision, and because neither proposal was finalized, existing obligations do not change. FinCEN said it will keep monitoring mixers for illicit use and cited a July 2025 President's Working Group report acknowledging lawful users may use mixers for financial privacy.

crypto.title: Henri Stern Steps In to Lead Stripe Crypto and Stablecoins
crypto.summary: Privy founder Henri Stern has taken on a dual role leading crypto and stablecoins at Stripe, tasked with building a stablecoin developer platform designed to be open, modular, and global by default. Stripe's existing client base shows the demand: Meta uses the rails to pay creators in real time, Ramp runs fiat and stablecoin flows in parallel for global expansion, and Deel routes contractor payouts worldwide, each requiring end-to-end orchestration rather than isolated point solutions. The platform integrates Bridge, Privy, Tempo, and Open USD together, treating fiat and crypto as interoperable layers rather than separate stacks businesses must rebuild from scratch. Stripe holds a conditional OCC national bank trust charter approval in the US along with MiCA and EMI licenses in Europe, placing it in a GENIUS Act-ready compliance posture.

crypto.title: Zcash's 25-Second Blocks Go Live on Public Testnet Ahead of Schedule
crypto.summary: Zcash activated its NU7 upgrade on the public testnet at block 4,465,026, cutting target block time from 75 seconds to 25 seconds and reducing three-confirmation finality from 225 seconds to 75 seconds. The upgrade splits fees 40/60 between miners and a reserve for future mining rewards, and reduces per-block rewards to one-third their current amount to maintain ZEC's issuance schedule despite the tripled block rate. NU7 also retires Sprout, Zcash's original shielded payment protocol, requiring holders to migrate funds before the planned November 5 mainnet activation. Both major node implementations, Zakura and Zebra, shipped compatible releases in the first two days of October, with developers targeting an October 20 decision on mainnet confirmation.

crypto.title: Polymarket Protocol V2
crypto.summary: Polymarket is replacing its Gnosis Conditional Tokens Framework (CTF) from 2019, which accumulated contract layers with each new feature, with Protocol V2: a ground-up rebuild that consolidates the stack into one ERC1155 positions contract, one pUSD collateral token, one exchange, and one router across all market types. A new OracleAggregator with pluggable resolution modules connects to UMA, Chainlink, and future oracle sources, while first-class bridging support for positions, collateral, and resolutions lays the infrastructure for multi-chain expansion. The protocol launches with four market types (Binary, Atomic Neg-risk, Incremental Neg-risk, and Combinatorial) and is upgradeable behind a governance process, enabling the team to ship features without disrupting existing integrations.

crypto.title: Chainalysis Used AI to Trace the $387M Bitget Hack Back to North Korea
crypto.summary: Chainalysis attributed the September 24 Bitget breach to North Korean actors, a $387M theft that pushed the DPRK's 2026 crypto total past $1 billion. Within three hours of the hack, attackers dispersed funds across Ethereum (49.7%), XRP (40.8%), Zcash (7.6%), and Tron (1.8%) in 23 transfers. Custom AI tools compressed what would have required 20+ hours of manual bridge reconciliation into under 10 minutes, with human investigators directing the analysis throughout. Attackers routed stolen XRP through cross-chain liquidity protocols to convert it into Bitcoin over roughly 36 hours before funds reached attacker-controlled addresses, avoiding direct exchange exposure.

crypto.title: Near Intents Recovers $3.8 Million After 48-Hour Ultimatum
crypto.summary: Near Intents recovered its full $3.8 million in stolen funds within 48 hours after General Manager Alex Shevchenko identified the attacker on-chain and issued a return deadline with an implicit deanonymization threat. The exploit targeted a flaw in how the platform's Omni deposit/withdrawal layer interacted with its main smart contract, forcing Near Intents to halt operations across its 35-blockchain cross-chain swap service. The attacker returned all funds and posted an on-chain message acknowledging fault and urging others to use bug bounties rather than exploits. The incident came days after Near Intents blocked a $50 million swap attempt linked to the $387.5 million Bitget breach, marking the platform's second high-profile security event within a week.

crypto.title: ZachXBT says he fronted $349,700 to infiltrate alleged launderers
crypto.summary: ZachXBT said he posed as a client and funded an address with 349,700 USDC to deal with a vendor called "Jimmy Green," alleging the network laundered over $1 billion across Lazarus-linked exploits, including most of the $1.5 billion Bybit hack. The intel helped trace a cluster of over $12 million in Bybit exploit funds, leading Tether to freeze 442,000 USDT, and he lost about 5% per order while operating the sting. He says he shared findings with law enforcement and has helped facilitate the freezing of $75 million tied to North Korean incidents since 2022.

crypto.title: Ondo launches onchain private-company exposure, starting with AI
crypto.summary: Ondo Private Markets will offer tokenized notes tied to the per-share value of selected private companies at qualifying liquidity events, starting with a pre-IPO AI firm whose notes are expected to begin 24/7 secondary-market trading this week. The notes are not shares and carry no ownership or shareholder rights, are obligations of the issuer, and are available only to eligible non-US investors, with robotics, cybersecurity, biotech, and infrastructure companies to follow. Ondo said its tokenized stocks and Treasurys platforms hold $3.7 billion in TVL with more than 1 million cumulative holders, while tokenized equities overall exceed $42 billion in market cap, about 35% of the $121 billion tokenized-asset market.

crypto.title: True Cashback Calculator accounts for caps, fees, and FX costs
crypto.summary: Headline crypto card cashback rates like "5%" ignore cashback caps, FX costs, card and subscription fees, spending limits, and reward conditions.

crypto.title: OKX and ICE file with the SEC to bring 63 NYSE stocks on-chain
crypto.summary: OKX and NYSE owner ICE filed with the SEC through their joint venture OKXICE to offer tokenized shares of 63 NYSE-listed companies, making them among the first major crypto exchange players to use the SEC's new tokenized stock trading rules.

crypto.title: Ethereum completes its first atomic transaction between L1 and L2
crypto.summary: Mainnet completed its first atomic transaction between L1 and an L2, meaning the two layers can coordinate within a single transaction rather than acting like separate networks.

crypto.title: CFTC Seeks Public Comment on Crypto Asset Rulemaking
crypto.summary: The CFTC published an Advanced Notice of Proposed Rulemaking seeking public comment on crypto asset transaction and market regulation, a formal pre-rulemaking step that precedes actual rule drafting.

it.title: The internet's DNS root key changes October 11
it.summary: The DNS root will switch to a new key-signing key on October 11, only the second such rollover ever. Most organizations need to do nothing, but anyone operating DNSSEC-validating resolvers should verify that their infrastructure trusts KSK-2024 or risk DNS resolution failures.

it.title: Lambda seeks up to $4 billion ahead of planned IPO
it.summary: Lambda reportedly seeks up to $4 billion at a $14.5 billion pre-money valuation before a planned 2027 IPO, with Coatue and Blackstone leading.

it.title: Atlassian warns of critical file access flaw in its datacenter products
it.summary: Atlassian has issued an urgent warning regarding a critical 9.3-rated arbitrary file access vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-21589, that affects multiple Data Center products, including Bitbucket and Confluence. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to access specific files within the web application root directory if they know the exact filename and path. Atlassian has released fixed versions and recommends immediately patching affected installations. Organizations unable to patch should restrict external access or apply the published mitigations.

it.title: Intel CIO: Don't just put chatbots on top of broken processes
it.summary: Intel CIO Cynthia Stoddard argues that companies should measure AI through business outcomes such as cycle-time improvements and ROI rather than tool adoption. Intel's approach combines employee training and experimentation with permission controls, data governance, MCP controls, and observability, while redesigning the underlying processes AI is meant to improve.

it.title: Enterprise security needs to start governing what AI agents do, not just what they can access
it.summary: Traditional access controls answer whether an identity has permission, but autonomous agents introduce a second question: whether a permitted action actually matches the user's intent. The piece argues for behavioral governance, sensitive-data controls, audit trails, and targeted human approval for high-impact actions rather than treating AI security as another SSO problem.

it.title: Inference Is the Most Important Market in Software
it.summary: AI inference could become a larger software market than databases, with spending projected to reach $350 billion by 2027. Rising inference costs will pressure software companies' gross margins, forcing them to improve efficiency through smaller models, better harnesses, and smarter routing techniques.

it.title: Atlassian expands OpenAI partnership for enterprise agents
it.summary: Atlassian and OpenAI expanded their partnership to combine OpenAI models with the Teamwork Graph, which connects company projects, documents, people, and decisions. The companies are also exploring Jira integrations for assigning work to agents, tracking progress, and reviewing results.

it.title: Google Docs can finally edit Markdown files natively
it.summary: Google Docs can now open, edit, comment on and collaboratively work with .md files without converting them into Google Docs, while Drive can render Markdown previews. The change is especially useful as AI agents and developer tools increasingly generate Markdown as a default working format.

it.title: Cloudflare Birthday Week 2026: Complete Launch Wrap-Up
it.summary: Cloudflare published a comprehensive wrap-up of 46 announcements made during its Birthday Week 2026 celebration. The updates span across open-source commitments, application security and post-quantum cryptography, economic models for the agentic Internet, developer platform tools, and performance and observability enhancements.

it.title: How to build an AI-native software factory
it.summary: Companies building AI-native software factories need managed environments, shared skills, cost controls, and validation systems to support fleets of autonomous coding agents. A four-step framework and six foundational platform components help teams start with low-risk tasks such as code reviews and migrations.

it.title: Software stocks hit 2026 highs as “SaaSpocalypse” fears fade
it.summary: US software stocks have climbed to fresh 2026 highs as strong results from companies including Salesforce and ServiceNow ease fears that AI would rapidly replace traditional SaaS. Analysts increasingly see AI as an enabler for established software vendors, although the longer-term threat from cheaper AI-built internal applications remains.

it.title: Docker does that?! Five Docker capabilities in one morning
it.summary: Docker demonstrated five modern Docker capabilities during a conference talk, highlighting features like AI-assisted containerization, Testcontainers for integration testing, Docker Scout for vulnerability scanning, Docker Hardened Images for pre-patched base images, and Docker Sandboxes for securing coding agents. The session aimed to update developers' mental models of Docker beyond simple packaging. All five steps are available via a browser-based workshop.

it.title: Orchestrating Disposable Browser
it.summary: Building a containerized disposable Browser as a Service infrastructure where logs are streamed from Docker to Python with specific tokens to strike a balance between speed and stability.

it.title: Tanium reworks its security operations platform around behavior-based detection
it.summary: Tanium is emphasizing endpoint behavior and rapid response to attacks that use stolen credentials and legitimate administrative tools rather than conventional malware.

it.title: Everyone into the Pool
it.summary: Evaluation of five PostgreSQL connection poolers—Pgpool-II, PgBouncer, RDS Proxy, PgCat, and PgDog—that compares their process models, pooling modes, and handling of session state.

hardware.title: A 1 MW AI data center in a shipping container, live in days
hardware.summary: Building a data center takes 3–5 years, and about a third of the power goes to cooling and building systems instead of compute. Runware's Sonic Pods skip all of it. Each pod is a complete AI inference data center in a 20 ft shipping container , trucked in and live in days: Up to 1,200 GPUs and 1 MW of compute, any GPU architecture Closed-loop liquid cooling on every GPU: 1.5 m³ of water, recirculated, none consumed Europe is live, US rollout underway Capacity is filling up. Reserve a pod or start on Serverless , billed by the second.

hardware.title: SpaceX seeks $40B Apollo-led debt financing to buy Nvidia chips
hardware.summary: The FT reports SpaceX is raising about $10 billion in bank loans and $30 billion in investment-grade debt to fund an Nvidia chip order, with Apollo leading and helping sell the debt to a broad investor base, and bond fund Pimco among lenders in talks. The deal is expected to close in 2027. It fits the pattern Nvidia flagged in August, when it disclosed its own SpaceX stake and a $500 billion Wall Street financing push, with chip purchases increasingly funded by debt and equity ties to the buyer. Reuters could not independently verify the report, and SpaceX, Apollo, Nvidia, and Pimco haven't commented.

hardware.title: Ghost launches a personal AI computer
hardware.summary: Ghost opened pre-orders for Core, a $3,499 screenless computer with an Nvidia RTX Pro 4000 SFF Blackwell GPU. The device runs preinstalled AI models locally and gives users access through a phone app. Ghost raised an $11 million seed round and plans to ship the first batch in late October.

hardware.title: Synopsys and OpenAI team up on GPT-Synopsys, a frontier model that runs EDA tools like an engineer
hardware.summary: GPT-Synopsys is an OpenAI frontier model trained and tuned to operate Synopsys' EDA tools directly, covering PPA optimization, timing closure, and verification. Engineers hand it an objective, and agents run the tools, interpret the results, make changes, and loop until there's a verified outcome to review. It runs on OpenAI-hosted infrastructure and plugs into Synopsys.ai and the Autopilot agentic platform. OpenAI licenses Synopsys' tools to train the model, paying a training subscription fee, and the two companies then share revenue based on how well the model improves chip designs, an unusual structure that ties both to the results. Synopsys says customer design data stays protected and won't be used to train the frontier model, and the bundled service covers compute, the model, and EDA licenses.

hardware.title: Designing chips for extreme environments
hardware.summary: Engineers must test chips against combined radiation, thermal shock, vibration, and other stresses rather than qualify each condition alone. Arizona State University pairs a radiation source with a cryostat to test devices at 77 Kelvin. Digital twins can model package and system behavior, but physical tests still check whether those predictions hold.

hardware.title: ScaRF-SLAM: Scale-Consistent Reconstruction with Feed-Forward Models and Classical Visual SLAM
hardware.summary: ScaRF-SLAM is a dense visual mapping system that pairs the reliability of classical visual SLAM with modern feed-forward geometric foundation models for 3D scene reconstruction. By decoupling camera tracking from dense depth estimation and optimizing scale consistency across submaps, it achieves globally accurate 3D maps across diverse sensor configurations. For perception engineers and autonomy developers, this framework provides a practical way to produce metric-scale environmental maps in real time without sacrificing tracking stability.

hardware.title: RoboParty demonstrates the RP1 humanoid
hardware.summary: RoboParty demonstrated RP1 recovering its balance after visitors pushed or kicked it at IROS. The platform combines actuator modules, robot hardware, and reinforcement-learning motion control, with peak joint torque up to 160 Nm. RoboParty plans to release more control software, simulation tools, and hardware details, so its full open-source roadmap remains in progress.

hardware.title: Google faces scrutiny over Finnish data-center clearing
hardware.summary: Finnish authorities are investigating allegations that Google's local operator cleared over 300 hectares of forest before a required environmental assessment. A conservation group has requested a suspension of work near Muhos. Google says the tree felling complied with forestry requirements and that it protected high-value nature zones.

hardware.title: OpenTPU Full-Stack Open-Source AI Accelerator
hardware.summary: OpenTPU is a complete, open-source AI accelerator project that packages custom SystemVerilog RTL, instruction set architecture, a bit-exact simulator, and a compiler into a single accessible repository. The design runs modern quantized language models directly on cost-effective Kintex-7 FPGA PCIe cards, matching simulation results bit for bit. This architecture provides embedded systems designers and compute engineers an invaluable end-to-end reference for deploying and tailoring custom neural network hardware without relying on proprietary black-box tooling.

hardware.title: Meta develops compressed RAM "CRAM" for Linux
hardware.summary: Meta's Gregory Price presented hardware-offloaded compression at Linux Plumbers.

hardware.title: Hex Open-Source Hexapod Robot Platform
hardware.summary: Hex is an open-source, six-legged robot platform designed to give makers and developers an accessible foundation for building and testing legged locomotion.

hardware.title: AMD says it will substantially increase chip supply in 2027
hardware.summary: Lisa Su said supply grew through 2026.

hardware.title: Trump announces nearly $7B Anduril submarine shipyard deal in Baltimore
hardware.summary: Anduril will invest $3.7 billion to build a two-million-square-foot "software-defined" shipyard at Sparrows Point, the former Bethlehem Steel site near Baltimore, and the Navy separately awarded it a $2.9 billion "Arsenal 2" contract with payments tied to production outcomes, bringing the package to roughly $6.6 billion.
